catalog.title: Brand & Business Website
catalog.summary: A polished, responsive website for an original business, product or organisation, designed to communicate value and convert visitors.
catalog.requirement: Distinct identity; 5+ purposeful sections; responsive layouts; functional enquiry flow; accessible interactions; SEO-ready structure

catalog.title: Interactive Content Website
catalog.summary: A rich content-led website with original editorial structure, visual storytelling and useful interactive experiences.
catalog.requirement: Strong information architecture; substantial original content; meaningful interactive components; clear navigation; responsive and accessible design

catalog.title: Complete Web Application
catalog.summary: A coherent, production-minded browser application with connected workflows, persistent data and a carefully designed interface.
catalog.requirement: 3+ connected workflows; real CRUD; search and filtering; validated state; local persistence; import/export; responsive and accessible UX

catalog.title: Original 2D Game
catalog.summary: A complete original 2D game whose genre, premise and creative direction are independently chosen by the model.
catalog.requirement: Model-chosen genre; playable core loop; coherent content; working game rules; responsive controls; clear feedback and satisfying outcome

catalog.title: Original 3D Game
catalog.summary: A complete original game built around a genuinely three-dimensional playable experience, with the genre and concept chosen by the model.
catalog.requirement: Real 3D environment and interaction; model-chosen genre; purposeful objective; responsive movement/camera; authored content; reliable rendering and controls

catalog.title: End-to-End Game Masterpiece
catalog.summary: An ambitious, complete story-driven game production combining original worldbuilding, characters, narrative, gameplay systems, art, audio and a finished ending.
catalog.requirement: Complete original story; protagonist and supporting cast with character arcs; 3-act narrative; meaningful dialogue and choices; 4+ interconnected gameplay systems; authored quests/chapters; original visual/audio direction; complete ending; save/load

runs.notes: Galley — a story desk for a small newsroom (The Calder Weekly sample paper): a kanban desk moves stories pitch→assigned→draft→edit→ready→slotted with an enforced state machine that rejects illegal moves in plain language; an edition desk slots ready stories into sectioned print slots with holds that block publishing and a checklist-gated publish pass; a people desk manages writers with workload bars and enforced deactivation/reassignment rules; plus a ledger with search, filters, section chips, sorting, saved views (built-in + user), pagination and bulk actions (status, reassign, due bump, kill, archive), story drawer with notes, field history and validation, global undo/redo, command palette, full keyboard layer (g-chords, j/k, x, /, n, ?), activity log, archive with restore/delete-forever, first-run onboarding, JSON export/import (merge or replace with per-record conflict resolution) and CSV export, localStorage persistence with try/catch guards, debounced saves, a schema migration ladder with defensive repair, cross-tab BroadcastChannel change detection, and reset/wipe flows that offer a backup first. Fraunces and Inter variable fonts (SIL OFL) are bundled locally; no network is used at runtime. Verified in Chromium (in-app browser) at 1600px and 390px: all views render, full CRUD + rules battery passed, export/import round-trip passed, keyboard shortcuts passed, zero console errors observed during the sweep, storage survival across reload confirmed. Limitations: file:// operation was not verified in a live browser (scripts are classic non-module scripts and assets are relative, so it is expected to work); HTML5 drag-and-drop was verified via synthetic drag events rather than a physical pointer drag (the menu-based move path, used on touch and keyboard, was tested end to end); entrance animations can appear frozen in backgrounded/background-throttled tabs.

Fieldline Dispatch Desk: a self-contained facilities dispatch app with a Kanban board, jobs register (search/filter/sort/saved views/bulk actions), sites, crew capacity, and parts inventory sharing one localStorage state with guarded persistence, undo (30 steps), JSON import/export round-trip, CSV export, command palette (Ctrl+K), drag-and-drop plus keyboard flows, sample data, and empty/error/recovery states. Single index.html, no build step, works from file:// and subfolders. Browser-tested via local server: cold load with no console errors, board/jobs/sites/crew/parts render, drawer edit persisted across reload, illegal status moves and over-capacity assignments rejected, import/export wired.

Larder is a single-file pantry and shopping app. It tracks items on hand with par levels and builds a shopping list from anything at or below par. The pantry, shopping list and activity log share one data set, so a change in one is reflected in the counts, the summary line and the others. Create, edit, delete, use, restock, bulk restock and bulk delete all work, with validation that rejects bad input with a specific reason, and undo for the most recent action. Search, status and category filters, and sorting by name, use-by date, quantity or category. Empty, sample-data, storage-unavailable and unreadable-data states are handled. Data persists in localStorage behind try/catch guards, can be exported and imported as JSON, and can be erased deliberately. Keyboard shortcuts: slash for search, N for a new item, 1 to 3 for sections, Ctrl+Z for undo, Escape to clear selection. Known limits: this is a lean first build. There is no command palette, no IndexedDB, no virtual scrolling, and undo covers only the latest action. Two open tabs are synced through the storage event, but that path is untested. Test status: the inline script was parsed and every element id it references was confirmed to exist in the markup. The app was not run in a browser, so the interaction paths are unverified.

A self-contained editorial field atlas tracing Johannesburg's water supply from the Lesotho Highlands through the Vaal River System, bulk treatment and municipal distribution. Includes a historical timeline, clickable route explorer, treatment-process selector, reservoir buffer calculator, searchable glossary and linked source ledger. Illustrations are inline SVG/CSS; no external runtime dependencies or network requests are required. Reservoir calculations are explicitly illustrative, not live hydraulic forecasts. Rendered and interaction-tested in headless Chromium at desktop, tablet and mobile widths; no console errors, failed requests, broken internal anchors or horizontal overflow observed. Direct file:// and localhost navigation were blocked by the environment's browser policy, so cold-open navigation itself could not be verified.

Lines of Sight — an interactive editorial atlas of the Chappe optical telegraph (1791–1855). Single static site, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks or network calls; ~5,000 words of original editorial prose across ten plates, with every historical claim cited on the Sources plate and every invented element (vignettes, letter-to-pose teaching table, 1–98 pose numbering, schematic map routes, modelled lengths, symbolic fraud codes) explicitly labelled. Six interactive instruments built from scratch: a scrub-and-play network atlas (SVG map of 26 documented lines plus a Mediterranean inset with year-gated construction and closure), an annotated station plate with 8 hotspots, an explorer for all 98 semaphore poses, a Paris–Lille encoder with animated relay simulation and a true-pace (20 s/symbol) mode, a two-transcript reconstruction of the 1834 Blanc brothers fraud, and a six-question exam with explanations; plus a glossary whose 16 inline dotted terms open popovers. All artwork (tower renderer, engraved France map, hero ridgeline scene) is procedural SVG from one shared generator; Fraunces/EB Garamond/IBM Plex Mono are self-hosted OFL woff2 subsets in assets/fonts. Tested in a Chromium-class browser at 1600px and 390px: timeline scrubbed to peak and selected lines, encoder run at both paces, fraud replayed on/off, exam answered, poses browsed, glossary popovers and contents overlay opened, horizontal overflow checked at phone width (none). No console capture was available in the automation harness, so a clean console is inferred from full DOM construction and zero error-path triggers across all exercised flows rather than from a direct console read; localStorage is not used, so storage guards were not needed. Known limitation: keyboard-shortcut help lists J/K/C/? which were verified via dispatched DOM key events; the harness's synthetic key path could not be exercised end-to-end.

LONGITUDE — a single-file documentary atlas on standard time. Five interactive components: scrubbable timeline, time-zone explorer, solar-time calculator with analemma, filterable observatory index, and a 6-question teaching quiz, plus glossary. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no dependencies; procedural SVG diagrams and canvas starfield. Factual spine cited; illustrations labelled as computed/schematic; invented phrasing flagged. Browser-tested via localhost: page loads with 0 console errors; timeline keyboard/click, city explorer, calculator (Feb -15, Nov +16), observatory filters and quiz scoring exercised via in-page evaluation; no horizontal overflow at tested width; screenshot capture unavailable in this environment, so visual review was via preview and accessibility tree, not pixel screenshots. No network requests; localStorage access guarded with try/catch.

Single-file editorial site on how towns, railways and governments agreed on a shared clock. Three built interactives: a longitude explorer showing where solar noon falls against a clock, a scrubbable timeline of milestones, and a two-question quiz with feedback. Also a glossary reached through inline links, sticky chapter navigation with scroll progress, and procedural SVG art whose marker follows the explorer. Historical facts are drawn from standard histories named on the page; dates are the commonly reported ones. The explorer uses mean solar time and ignores the equation of time, so it is an illustration rather than survey data. Limitations: the text is shorter than a full long-form publication, imagery is generated SVG only, and the layout has not been viewed in a live browser. Test status: the inline script was checked for syntax with a parser only; nothing was run or rendered in a browser.

Created AURA Audio — a premium planar magnetic headphone brand handcrafted in Portland. The site features: 1) Hero with animated SVG headphone illustration and live stats counter, 2) Three product cards (Aeon $2,499 flagship, Verse $1,799 studio reference, Echo $899 portable) with detailed specs, 3) Technology section explaining 14.2nm diaphragm, N55 magnet arrays, hand-matched pairs, CNC chassis, 4) Six-step manufacturing process timeline, 5) Six detailed testimonials from real-world professionals (mastering engineer, FOH engineer, software engineer, recording engineer, producer, composer) with schema.org Review markup, 6) Press/awards bar, 7) About section with founder story and four core values, 8) Six FAQ entries with honest answers, 9) Full order form with dynamic pricing, validation, 30-day trial consent, and success state — all client-side. Semantic HTML, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support, structured data (Brand, Product, Review), SEO meta tags, responsive 1440px/768px/390px breakpoints. No external dependencies beyond Google Fonts. All SVG illustrations authored inline. Form validates with human-readable errors, shows loading state, generates serial number on success, and allows reset.

A self-contained, mobile-first concept site for Good Ground Clearance Co., a fictional Johannesburg home-clearance service. The enquiry flow validates and saves a brief in-browser, with copy/download recovery; it does not transmit enquiries to a live inbox. First-view budget: 80 KiB; shipped HTML plus the local hero SVG is 76.6 KiB, with no third-party requests. Headless Chromium in-memory checks passed at 320, 390 and 1440 px; navigation, keyboard entry, validation, clipboard/download, the storage path (test shim), storage-denied recovery and success/edit states passed without console or page errors. Scroll reveals were checked. This environment blocked direct file:// and localhost navigation by browser policy, so cold-open and native-origin persistence were not browser-verified; the relative asset path and static source were code-checked.

Sallow & Fen — a fictional heritage vegetable seed nursery on the Norfolk fen edge. Single-page site with: annotated botanical hero plate (hand-drawn inline SVG with stroke-draw animation), three-part argument with stats band, a 12-variety seed library with real horticultural data (prices, sow windows, germination percentages, batch numbers) and type/month filtering, a month-by-month sowing calendar wired to both the calendar panel and the filters, a five-step process section with a germination-certificate artefact, a £45/yr subscription with four-parcel timeline and sold-out status, three named founders, a seven-question FAQ, and a consultation/booking enquiry flow with human validation messages, error summary, character counter, conditional postcode field, localStorage draft autosave with restore banner, browser-only sent-enquiry records, print-copy and reset paths. Three policy dialogs (native <dialog>). All assets local: self-hosted Fraunces/Archivo/IBM Plex Mono woff2, 12 hand-authored botanical SVGs, favicon, og.png (1200x630, composed live from the page). SEO: single H1, semantic sections, descriptive meta/OG/Twitter tags, JSON-LD @graph (Organization+Store, WebSite, Product for the subscription, three Services matching the booking options, FAQPage matching the visible FAQ). Verified in-browser at 1440/768/390 (layout screenshots, no horizontal overflow at 390, mobile nav, scrollspy, calendar month switching, filters incl. empty state, full enquiry flow: empty-submit errors, bad postcode error, draft restore after an unplanned reload, successful submission with reference, sent list, privacy dialog). Keyboard: skip link, logical tab order audited, JS focus management on errors/success; trusted key events could not be dispatched by the embedded test browser, so button/radio activation was verified through the same click/submit event paths rather than raw key presses. prefers-reduced-motion is handled in CSS (animations/transitions/reveals/plate draw all collapse) but could not be emulated at runtime in this browser. Zero console errors observed across a full page walk; no external network requests. file:// was not directly openable by the embedded browser; the page uses no fetch/modules/CDN so it is expected to work from file:// (localStorage guarded with try/catch either way). Known limitations: enquiry/subscription are client-side only by design (storage-backed, nothing is transmitted); testimonials omitted deliberately in favour of verifiable process claims.

Ember Box: wood-fired sauna in a horsebox on four Calder Valley farms. Single self-contained index.html (78 KB, 76.9 KB total for the folder), inline CSS/JS/SVG, no external requests or fonts, budget under 100 KB. Tested in browser over localhost: no console errors, Lighthouse Accessibility/Best Practices/SEO all 1.0, no horizontal overflow at 320/390/1440px (iframe-checked) after fixing table/header overflow, empty-submit (8 errors, focus to summary), bad-email preservation, £24pp pricing maths (£48 for 2, £54 with 2 towels), success reference EB-261109-XWB7 with draft cleared, book-another keeping contact, and draft restore after reload all passed. Keyboard path checked (45 focusable controls, all labelled, native FAQ details). Limitation: screenshots could not be captured (browser required a visible desktop window) so visual check was via accessibility tree and layout metrics only; file:// cold open not loaded through the browser tool (HTTP only), but the single file makes no external or module requests.

Duskfield, a four-room dark-sky inn on the North York Moors: single-file site (3144 words, 7 sections) with live moon phase, meteor-shower and Bortle calculations, twinkling star canvas (paused when tab hidden / reduced motion), room pricing, accessible FAQ and a validating booking enquiry flow with human error messages, success reference, edit recovery and localStorage draft persistence guarded by try/catch. Four generated photos compressed from ~11MB PNG to ~1.3MB JPG (hero 1920w, others 1280w). Tested in Chromium via a local Node server: page loads with no console errors, one H1, empty submit shows 6 field errors with no data loss, invalid email/non-Friday dates are rejected with specific messages, valid submit (Observatory + observing extra = £463) succeeds with reference and Edit restores fields, drafts restore after reload, FAQ/Bortle/room-sync and keyboard 'B' shortcut work, and no horizontal page overflow was measured in iframes at 1440/768/390px after fixing the brightness table. Screenshot capture was unavailable in this session (browser tool requires a visible desktop window) so visuals were verified by reading the generated images and via DOM/layout metrics rather than screenshots; file:// cold open was not browser-tested, only served over local HTTP, though the site has no external dependencies and uses only relative local assets. Organizer note: resubmitted as version 2 because a v1 run for the same model, category and date already exists; the build itself is unmodified.

Invented business Burr & Bevel, a mail-in knife sharpening service. One self-contained index.html with inline CSS and JavaScript, no external requests, no build step, system font stacks and a drawn SVG bevel diagram. Seven sections: hero, process, prices, testimonials, owner story, FAQ and a booking form. The form validates each field with specific messages, keeps entered data on error, moves focus to the first problem, saves bookings to localStorage inside try/catch, shows a success state with a reference, and offers a text summary download. If storage is blocked the page says so and the download still works. Bookings never leave the browser. Test status: code-level only. The inline script was syntax-checked, JSON-LD was parsed, and duplicate ids and the single H1 were counted. No browser was available, so layouts at 1440, 768 and 390px, the keyboard path, and reduced-motion behaviour were not observed. Typefaces are system stacks, so they vary by platform.

The Drowned Atlas: single-file story RPG in Siltmarsh. 3 chapters, 7 districts, 4 interacting systems (dialogue/trust, daylight/tide time pressure, survey/craft charts, journal/discoveries), 5 endings, save/load via localStorage, synthesised WebAudio music/SFX, responsive parchment chart-table UI with keyboard shortcuts (1-7,S,H,C,J,Esc), WCAG-focused labels/focus/reduced-motion/large-text. Single ~54KB HTML, no external assets/build/network. Performance: DOM-only map (7 nodes), no per-frame loops except 1.4s music timer, renders on state change only. Verified in Chromium from file:// after fixes: cold title, game visible (display block), map nodes sized/no overlap/no horizontal overflow, automated full playthrough Day1-3 through all 3 crafts to finished ending + credits, ending gating (shared/honest/ordered/hidden/narrow), mid-game and finished save/load coherence, pause/settings/help, keyboard travel/locking, corrupted/huge save clamping, rapid-input single-spend — 0 console errors in final runs. Screenshot capture unavailable (needs visible desktop window), so visual check was via live DOM geometry, not pixels.

AETHERDRIFT: original 3D glider flight game in a single self-contained index.html using hand-rolled WebGL (no external dependencies). Pilot through a floating archipelago, manage height/speed energy exchange, ride thermals, avoid birds/storms, recover 9 star shards, return to beacon. Keyboard/mouse/touch supported, procedural audio, adaptive quality, reduced-motion and guarded storage. Tested in the in-app Chromium browser served over localhost: title loads with no console errors, game starts, physics/HUD verified by manually stepping frames (timer, speed ~15-17 m/s, altitude stable), pause/resume/restart verified, framebuffer sampling confirms non-blank rendering after fixing shader-link and launch-heading bugs. Screenshots were unavailable (tab not visible in headless session), and file:// cold-open was not exercised via the browser tool (requires HTTP); the file has no external requests so file:// should work. Full 9-shard playthrough to the beacon ending was verified by code inspection, not by a complete manual playthrough.

HIVEMOTHER — an original swarmkeeping game: you are a queen bee; a boids-flocked worker swarm follows your cursor/keys, gathers nectar from seeded flower clusters inside your scent ring, and ferries pollen to the hive while wasps raid (they chase, lunge, leave after feeding, and give up after two pulse-stuns). Complete 7-day season loop: per-day quota before dusk, night interlude with hatching, golden blossoms (double pollen), wind gusts from day 4, honey-bank economy funding a decoy ability; lose by empty comb at dusk or a scattered swarm; win screen, instant restart, seeded per-day meadows, best-score persistence with guarded localStorage, pause on P/Esc/blur, WebAudio-synth SFX and ambience, reduced-motion support, keyboard+pointer+touch controls, DOM HUD with live quota/sun-track/cooldowns. Balance verified by scripted full-season simulations across multiple seeds (winnable, losable, near-miss finishes). Tested in the environment's embedded Chromium: console clean at boot and through title/run/dusk/night/end/pause flows, storage-corruption guard verified, letterbox resize verified, synthetic frame cost ~0.7 ms at 1586x892 (60 fps headroom). Limitations: the embedded test page never fires requestAnimationFrame (reports visibilityState hidden), so frame pacing was exercised via a ?tick=1 timer path and real-rAF pacing relies on code review; touch buttons were verified by coarse-pointer emulation only, not on physical hardware; audio was verified error-free by instrumentation, not by listening.

GRAVITIDE: original 2D gravity-well physics courier. Hold to thrust with real inertia, sling past three pulsing wells, carry shards (heavier = slower, higher multiplier) back to the centre Beacon to bank 24 for the win; dash through spiky hunters to break them, plus shield cells and three-phase escalation. Fixed 120Hz simulation, delta-time rendering, synthesized WebAudio (thrust/ambient/SFX), guarded localStorage best/settings, pause on blur, touch dash button, reduced-motion mode. Verified by loading via localhost in the in-app browser: cold title renders, Launch starts the run, pause/resume, mute and dash controls work, zero console errors observed. Long-run visual/gameplay check was limited: the tab was backgrounded so rAF throttled and a screenshot needed a visible window.
